key_terms.المْ: Disjointed letters (Alif, Lam, Mim) appearing at the beginning of several Quranic chapters.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the disjointed letters Alif Lam Mim in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the disjointed letters (Al-Huruf al-Muqatta'at) at the opening of Surah As-Sajdah are often interpreted as divine oaths or abbreviations referring to the Prophet Muhammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, highlighting the chapter's focus on the humility of the believers in prostration. This opening serves as a rhetorical challenge to the disbelievers, asserting the Quran's divine origin despite its use of familiar Arabic script, thereby reinforcing the concept of I'jaz (inimitability). The placement of these letters before a chapter detailing the signs of God in creation and the hereafter underscores the link between linguistic miracle and cosmic truth.
